transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Fitzgerald, thank you for coming back in to see me today. I have something very difficult to discuss with you regarding the procedure we did on your arm.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is something wrong? I've just been feeling so exhausted. Arthur always told me to be careful with these clinic visits.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a lot to take in, and I want to be completely honest with you. I made a mistake during the repair of your laceration. I didn't check if the anaesthetic had fully taken effect before I started the stitching, and as a result, the repair was done without enough numbing agent.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I... I remember it hurting. I thought I was just being a baby. I didn't want to make a fuss.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You weren't being a baby at all. It was my responsibility to ensure you were comfortable and numb, and I failed to do that. I am deeply sorry for the pain I caused you and for my oversight.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh dear. I just... everything has been so hard since Arthur passed. I can't seem to get a grip on anything.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It sounds like everything feels very overwhelming right now, especially while you're missing him.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It does. It really does. But why does it still feel strange? My hand doesn't feel right today.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is what I need to explain. Because the area wasn't properly numbed, the trauma of the procedure and the reaction to the pain caused some inflammation that has impacted the nerve in your wrist. In plain terms, the nerve is compressed, which is why you're feeling that numbness and weakness. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I think so. Compressed. Like it's being squeezed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Exactly. I want to make sure I'm being clear. Do you have any questions about how that happened?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why didn't you just stop when I flinched?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There is no excuse for that. I should have been paying closer attention to your reactions. I took my eye off the goal of your comfort, and I take full responsibility for that. I am so sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Arthur would be so cross. He always looked after me. Now I'm left with this... this shaking hand. Am I going to be able to knit again? I make sweaters for the grandchildren.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know how important those sweaters are for your family. To be honest with you, because of the degree of the nerve injury, there is a significant chance that your dexterity won't fully return to how it was before. I cannot promise that you will be able to knit exactly as you did.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No. No, that can't be right. I can't lose that too.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is devastating to hear. I am sitting here with you, and I recognize how unfair this is.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel so alone.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see how much this hurts, not just the hand, but the feeling of losing another piece of your routine. We are going to stay with you through every step of this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do we even do now? Is it just broken?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have a very specific plan to try and improve the outcome. First, I have already coordinated with the neurology department. You have an appointment for an EMG scan this Thursday at 10:00 AM to see exactly how the nerve is conducting.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thursday. I'll have to ask my daughter to drive me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That would be a good idea. After we get those results on Friday, you and I will meet again—I've blocked out an hour on my calendar for you—to decide if we start physical therapy or a surgical release. For your part, I want you to keep the wrist in the brace I'm giving you now, but only during the night.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Night only. I can do that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I also want to tell you what I am doing to make sure this never happens to another patient. I have filed a formal incident report, and I am meeting with my attending physician and the department head tomorrow morning to change our protocol. We are implementing a mandatory "pain check" verbal confirmation before any suturing begins.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're changing the rules because of me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. Your experience is a reminder of where I failed, and using this to protect other patients is the only way I can begin to make this right.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want my hand back.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I wish I could give it back to you right now. We will do everything humanly possible to recover as much function as we can. Do you feel okay with the plan for Thursday and Friday?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I think so. I just need to call my daughter.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Please take all the time you need. I'll stay right here with you until you've made that call.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to express grief and frustration without interruption and maintains a regulated, patient pace throughout.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn, used lay language ('compressed'), checked comprehension twice, and avoided false reassurance regarding knitting.

A.justification: Direct apologies used multiple times, full personal responsibility taken, and accountability maintained when questioned about flinching.

R.justification: Named specific emotions ('overwhelming', 'devastating') and engaged with the patient's personal mentions of her late husband and grandchildren.

T.justification: Provided specific steps (EMG scan) with timelines (Thursday 10am, Friday meeting), a patient role (nightly brace), and a prevention plan (mandatory pain check).
